ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows that JKMN is a rectangle: J is at the upper left, K is at the upper right, M is at the lower right, N is at the lower left, and right angles are marked at J and M in the figure. Two diagonals JM and NK are both drawn and intersect at the interior point Q; among them, NQ and QK are the two segments of diagonal NK. Reasoning: the diagonals of a rectangle bisect each other, so Q is the midpoint of NK, therefore NQ = QK. Given in the problem NQ = 2x + 3, QK = 5x - 9, obtain 2x + 3 = 5x - 9, solving gives 12 = 3x, so x = 4. Substituting gives QK = 5(4) - 9 = 11, NQ = 2(4) + 3 = 11. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other, so each half-diagonal is equal, therefore JQ = QK = 11.

Since rectangle diagonals are congruent and bisected at the same point, each half-diagonal is equal, so JQ=QK=11.
